mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.25% in the prior month does not lead to positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 7.5% signals improving labor market conditions, which increases consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 7.5%, the S&P 500 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the t-test of the mean return in triggered periods vs. baseline is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where both HOUST exceeds 750 and RSAFS exceeds 400000, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is negative.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions and rising consumer spending, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth above 100k in the prior month does not lead to positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A reading of industrial production (INDPRO) above 100 (2017=100) indicates a strengthening manufacturing sector, which signals economic expansion and positive corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO exceeds 100, the S&P 500 fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the mean return in triggered periods is not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong economic growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth rate > 1.5%), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns as corporate earnings rise, leading to a 60-day positive return.
failure_condition: In strong GDP growth regimes (GDPC1 > 1.5% q/q), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% signals rising inflation, which typically leads to Federal Reserve tightening and negative equity returns, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
